The base in two halves

The one-piece base is 208 mm across, which is too big for the A1 mini. This version is the same base cut into two identical halves that bolt together. These are the real meshes from the print file. Drag to turn the view, scroll or pinch to zoom.

Putting it together

  1. Print frame_base_half.stl twice, flat on the bed as it sits. No supports.
  2. Lay both halves on a flat table and push the seam closed.
  3. Fit the four M3 × 10 bolts through the ears and tighten the nuts. On the two outer joints, put the bolt head on the side nearer the centre.
  4. Screw the pedestal on from underneath, then add the towers. Once the towers are on, a screwdriver cannot reach the outer bolts.
Checked in the model, not yet on a printer

The script checks the two-piece base against the pedestal, the motors and the towers at both ends of their travel, and finds no collisions. It is somewhat less stiff than the one-piece base, and the two middle ears stand in front of two of the pedestal's four cable openings.
